title: Relative clauses / participles
subtitle: Defining and non-defining clauses, relative pronouns, and participle clauses

blocks.text: Relative clauses give us extra information about something or someone, or identify which particular thing or person we are talking about. They are often introduced by the following words.

rows.example: Did you see the documentary **which** was on TV last night?

rows.use: who (for people, and animals when we want to give them a personality)
rows.example: Nina Cole, **who** is appearing in concert in Leeds this week, is rehearsing with me in the studio.
Do you remember the summer **when** we met?
This is the village **where** they filmed the opening scenes.
That's the reason **why** the album became so popular.

rows.use: whom (for people as the object of the relative clause)
rows.example: Is that the woman **whom** we saw at the gallery yesterday?
My first guest is Clara Voss, **whose** career began in the late nineties.

blocks.text: When the relative pronoun (**who**, **which**, etc.) is the subject of the relative clause, you do not need another subject.

blocks.correct: I admire Lena Ortiz, **who** always works hard on her films.
blocks.incorrect: I admire Lena Ortiz, **who she** always works hard on her films.

blocks.text: **Whom** is quite formal. It is natural in informal English to use **who** instead of **whom**, even when it is the object of the relative clause. After a preposition, however, we always use **whom**. Informally, we usually put the preposition at the end of the clause and use **who**.

blocks.correct: Is that the actor **who** we saw at the cinema yesterday?
blocks.incorrect: Is that the actor **whom he** we saw at the cinema yesterday?

blocks.intro: Formal **whom** after a preposition vs informal **who** with the preposition at the end:
items: Buster Keaton was a comic genius **to whom** later performers owe a great deal.
Buster Keaton was a comic genius **who** later performers owe a great deal **to**.

blocks.text: **Where** can be replaced by a preposition + **which**. Less formally, we put the preposition at the end of the clause. The same pattern works with **when** / **in which**.

items: The studio **where / in which** I first acted is somewhere around here.
We can do the same thing with **when**.
Do you know the year **when / in which** the first western was made?

blocks.text: Non-defining relative clauses simply give us more information about something or someone. The sentence makes complete sense without the relative clause.

rows.use: To give extra information about something or someone
rows.example: Ray Watson, **who** starred in Night Train, is considering making a film based on the life of Einstein.

blocks.text: Non-defining relative clauses are separated from the rest of the sentence by commas.

blocks.correct: Megamonsters, **which** was filmed in New York, is a very disappointing film.
blocks.incorrect: Megamonsters which was filmed in New York is a very disappointing film.

blocks.text: We cannot leave out the word which introduces the relative clause and we cannot use the word **that** instead.

blocks.correct: Megamonsters, **which** was filmed in New York, is a very disappointing film.
blocks.incorrect: Megamonsters, **that** was filmed in New York, is a very disappointing film.

blocks.text: **Which** can refer back to the whole of the sentence, not just to one noun.

items: We finally got tickets for the concert, **which** was very lucky. (Getting the tickets was lucky — not the concert itself.)

blocks.text: Defining relative clauses tell us which one of a group of things or people we are talking about. The sentence doesn't usually make complete sense without the relative clause.

rows.use: To tell us which one of a group of things or people we are talking about
rows.example: The book **which** I've read was the best of all. The one **who** is wearing a blue shirt is Justin Timberlake, isn't it?

blocks.text: Defining relative clauses are not separated from the rest of the sentence by commas.

blocks.correct: This is the DVD **which** I told you about the other day.
blocks.incorrect: This is the DVD, **which** I told you about the other day.

blocks.text: We can also use **that** to introduce the relative clause.

items: This is the DVD **that** I told you about the other day.

blocks.text: We can often leave out the word which introduces the relative clause when it is the object of the clause.

items: This is the DVD I told you about the other day.

blocks.text: Notice that we do not need a preposition when we use **where** or **when**.

blocks.correct: The theatre **where** I first acted is somewhere around here.
blocks.incorrect: The theatre **where** I first acted **in** is somewhere around here.

blocks.correct: Do you know the year **when** the first western was made?
blocks.incorrect: Do you know the year **when** the first western was made **in**?

blocks.text: Present participles end in **-ing**. Past participles usually end in **-ed**, although there are many irregular verbs. Perfect participles are formed using **having** + past participle.

rows.use: To follow prepositions and conjunctions (present and perfect participles)
rows.example: **By appearing** in that cigarette advert, he damaged his acting career. **After playing / having played** video games all morning, I was really tired.

rows.use: To explain the reason for something (present and perfect participles)
rows.example: **Being** quite good-looking, Ralph decided to make a career as a model. **Having seen** the film before, I knew what was going to happen.

rows.use: To talk about actions happening at the same time (present participles)
rows.example: **Waiting** for the show to begin, I felt really nervous.

rows.use: To replace some relative clauses (present and past participles)
rows.example: Imagine being the person **directing** a big budget film! (= Imagine being the person **who is directing** a big budget film!) The person **chosen** for the part will be contacted by phone. (= The person **who is chosen** for the part will be contacted by phone.)

rows.use: To talk about past actions happening in sequence (perfect participles)
rows.example: **Having finished** my homework, I decided to go to the cinema.

rows.use: As an alternative passive form (past participles)
rows.example: **Made** to wait, the actor began to get very annoyed.

blocks.text: You have to be careful that the participle and the rest of the sentence both refer to the same subject.

blocks.correct: **Watching** TV, **I** saw a news report about Hollywood.
blocks.incorrect: **Watching** TV, a news report came on about Hollywood.

items.prompt: The minister, ___ was appointed last week, made no comment on the situation.
Isn't that the junction ___ the accident happened last night?
The blue whale, ___ weighs about 150 tonnes, is the largest animal on Earth.
There are several reasons ___ I don't want to see that play tonight.
This is the studio ___ I record most of my podcasts.
The new student in our class, ___ name is Alexandra, seems really nice.
The Titanic, ___ people said was unsinkable, sank on her maiden voyage.
items.explanation: Non-defining clauses take **which**, not **that**, and need commas.

items.prompt: All the people to ___ the e-mail was sent replied.
April 1st, ___ we play tricks on people, is known as April Fools' Day.
Harry Hill, ___ new series starts next week, is one of my favourite comedians.
A very popular breed of dog is the German Shepherd, ___ is often used as a guard dog.
Blackpool Tower, ___ was modelled on the Eiffel Tower, is a very well-known landmark.

exercises.title: B · Correct the relative pronoun
exercises.instruction: If the word in bold is already correct, write it again. If it is incorrect, write the correct relative pronoun or phrase.

items.prompt: November 5th was the day **which** Guy Fawkes tried to blow up Parliament.
There were none of my favourite biscuits left when I had a cup of tea, **that** was really annoying.
I've just got a new webcam **that** takes really clear pictures.
The Godfather was made by Francis Ford Coppola, **who's** daughter is also a film director.
Can you think of any reason **which** Cathy might be angry with me?
Here's a photo of the hotel **where we stayed in** when we were in Beijing.
items.explanation: Do not add a preposition after **where**.

items.prompt: How do you think the first man **whom** walked on the moon felt?
This is the first occasion **on which** the leaders of these two countries have met.
He is a person for **who** very few people feel much sympathy.
The moment **which** the hero suddenly appears from behind a tree is the best moment in the whole film.
I met a man **which** had a dog with only three legs.
My new school, **who** I moved to about a month ago, seems like quite a friendly place.

exercises.title: C · Rewrite as one sentence
exercises.instruction: Rewrite as one sentence using a relative clause.

items.prompt: My friend, Simon, plays the guitar. He has just released a CD.
acceptedAnswers: My friend, Simon, who has just released a CD, plays the guitar.
My friend Simon, who has just released a CD, plays the guitar.
My friend, Simon, who plays the guitar, has just released a CD.

items.prompt: Prince Charles is heir to the throne of England. His wife was Princess Diana.
acceptedAnswers: Prince Charles, whose wife was Princess Diana, is heir to the throne of England.
Prince Charles, who is heir to the throne of England, was married to Princess Diana.

items.prompt: Microsoft has a lot of power in the world of computers. That annoys some people.
acceptedAnswers: Microsoft has a lot of power in the world of computers, which annoys some people.
Microsoft, which has a lot of power in the world of computers, annoys some people.

items.prompt: The euro replaced a number of national currencies. It was introduced in January 2002.
acceptedAnswers: The euro, which was introduced in January 2002, replaced a number of national currencies.
The euro, which replaced a number of national currencies, was introduced in January 2002.

items.prompt: Friends ran for ten years. It is one of my favourite series.
acceptedAnswers: Friends, which ran for ten years, is one of my favourite series.
Friends, which is one of my favourite series, ran for ten years.

items.prompt: Venus is a very hot place. It is much closer to the Sun than the Earth is.
acceptedAnswers: Venus, which is much closer to the Sun than the Earth is, is a very hot place.
Venus, which is a very hot place, is much closer to the Sun than the Earth is.

items.prompt: Cricket is popular in many countries around the world. It is played between two teams of eleven.
acceptedAnswers: Cricket, which is played between two teams of eleven, is popular in many countries around the world.
Cricket, which is popular in many countries around the world, is played between two teams of eleven.

items.prompt: Parts of Buckingham Palace are open to the public. It is where the queen lives.
acceptedAnswers: Parts of Buckingham Palace, where the queen lives, are open to the public.
Buckingham Palace, which is where the queen lives, has parts that are open to the public.
Parts of Buckingham Palace, which is where the queen lives, are open to the public.

items.prompt: The greyhound is the fastest dog. It can reach speeds of over 65 kilometres an hour.
acceptedAnswers: The greyhound, which can reach speeds of over 65 kilometres an hour, is the fastest dog.
The greyhound, which is the fastest dog, can reach speeds of over 65 kilometres an hour.

items.prompt: 1984 was written by George Orwell. His real name was Eric Blair.
acceptedAnswers: 1984 was written by George Orwell, whose real name was Eric Blair.
1984, which was written by George Orwell, whose real name was Eric Blair, is a famous novel.

exercises.title: D · Find me a show that works
exercises.instruction: Write one word in each gap. Do not write **that** and do not leave any gaps blank.

items.prompt: I'm sure there was a reason (1) ___ I became a TV reviewer.
Maybe it was my love of classic shows (2) ___ kept me entertained as a child.
Or maybe it was the presenters (3) ___ seemed to promise an exciting world of glamour and showbiz.
To be honest, I've watched so many shows lately (4) ___ have bored me to tears that I've forgotten.
Take Kid Swap, for example, the new show (5) ___ Channel 7 hopes will revive their viewing figures.
The show takes kids (6) ___ parents have had enough and swaps them with kids from other families for two weeks.
The problem with this show is that I'm just not sure at (7) ___ it's aimed — parents or teenagers.
Parents (8) ___ watch this show will find it childish,
particularly at the moment (9) ___ one of the teenagers does nothing but complain.
Teenage viewers (10) ___ watch more than the first five minutes will soon get bored of the parents,
(11) ___ blame anybody but themselves for the situation.
This is definitely one idea (12) ___ should be put exactly where it belongs — in the bin!

exercises.title: E · Could you use that?
exercises.instruction: Look at the gaps in Exercise D. Could the gap also be completed with **that**?

items.prompt: Gap 1 (reason ___ I became…)
Gap 2 (shows ___ kept me entertained…)
Gap 3 (presenters ___ seemed to promise…)
Gap 4 (shows ___ have bored me…)
Gap 5 (the new show ___ Channel 7 hopes…)
Gap 6 (kids ___ parents have had enough…)
Gap 7 (not sure at ___ it's aimed…)
items.explanation: After a preposition we need **whom**, not **that**.

items.prompt: Gap 8 (Parents ___ watch this show…)
Gap 9 (the moment ___ one of the teenagers…)
Gap 10 (Teenage viewers ___ watch more than…)
Gap 11 (the parents, ___ blame anybody…)
items.explanation: This is a non-defining clause (after a comma), so **that** is not possible.

items.prompt: Gap 12 (one idea ___ should be put…)

exercises.title: F · Choose the correct answer
exercises.instruction: Choose the correct option to complete each conversation.

items.prompt: 'Who's that over there?' 'Oh, it's our new teacher, ___ just started work today.'
'Which CD did you get Marcus in the end?' 'I got him the one ___ said he really wanted to hear.'
'Who did you send a Valentine's card to?' 'I'm not telling you, but it was someone ___ name begins with B!'
'Have you seen Jason Green's latest film?' 'Is that the one in ___ joins the FBI?'
'Why do you like Tania so much?' 'Well, she's one of the few people to ___ I can really talk.'
'Why don't we go to Lionel's for dinner tonight?' 'Is that the new restaurant ___ has just opened on the other side of town?'
'Could you lend me some money?' 'I'd like you to give me one good reason ___ I should.'
'What do you want to do this summer?' 'I think we should go somewhere ___ has plenty of sun and sand.'

exercises.title: G · Can the relative pronoun be left out?
exercises.instruction: In defining relative clauses, we can often omit the relative pronoun when it is the object. Decide whether the relative pronoun in bold can be left out.

items.prompt: The number of options **that** are available to us is increasing all the time.
…with **which** to fill our leisure time…
items.explanation: After a preposition the pronoun cannot be omitted.

items.prompt: Previous generations, **who** lived before the electronic age, had musical instruments and card games.
items.explanation: Non-defining clauses never omit the pronoun, and **who** is the subject.

items.prompt: …card games **that** they played to pass the time…
…parents **whose** teenagers spend a lot of time on these activities…
…the effect **which** it is having on them…
…**which** is becoming more important as life becomes more stressful.
The television programmes **which** we watch…
…the computer games **that** we play all entertain us…
…people to **whom** they seem a complete waste of time…
Entertainment is something **which** we all need…
…as long as we're willing to pay, there will always be someone **who** is willing to provide it.

exercises.title: H · Circle the correct participle
exercises.instruction: Choose the correct word or phrase.

items.prompt: Before ___ Harriet, I never knew what real love was.
I'm sure that after ___ your exam, you'll feel a lot better.
Having ___ the letter, Peter printed it out.
___ through the window, I saw a strange man at the door.
I cooked dinner and, ___ that, I sat down to watch TV.
___ a noise outside, Janice went to investigate.
___ my notes, I couldn't revise properly for the test.
___ quite intelligent, Matt hopes to get into a good university.
___ the start of the film, I decided not to bother watching the rest of it.
After ___ her bed, Cherie had a shower.

exercises.title: I · Keep the meaning
exercises.instruction: Complete each sentence so that the meaning remains the same.

items.prompt:
I suddenly remembered where I'd left my keys when I was waiting for the bus.
**Waiting**
acceptedAnswers: Waiting for the bus, I suddenly remembered where I'd left my keys.
Waiting for the bus, I suddenly remembered where I had left my keys.

items.prompt:
I slipped because I was trying to run in the rain.
**Trying**
acceptedAnswers: Trying to run in the rain, I slipped.
Trying to run in the rain, I slipped over.

items.prompt:
I felt quite sorry for Tim when I saw him cry.
**Seeing**
acceptedAnswers: Seeing him cry, I felt quite sorry for Tim.
Seeing Tim cry, I felt quite sorry for him.

items.prompt:
John was depressed because he knew he was going to fail the exam.
**Knowing**
acceptedAnswers: Knowing he was going to fail the exam, John was depressed.
Knowing that he was going to fail the exam, John was depressed.

items.prompt:
The reason I'm quite good at basketball is that I'm quite tall.
**Being**
acceptedAnswers: Being quite tall, I'm quite good at basketball.
Being quite tall is the reason I'm quite good at basketball.
Being quite tall, I am quite good at basketball.

items.prompt:
Georgia didn't know any Japanese so she used a phrase book when she was there.
**Not**
acceptedAnswers: Not knowing any Japanese, Georgia used a phrase book when she was there.
Not knowing any Japanese, she used a phrase book when she was there.

items.prompt:
Ed can afford three holidays abroad each year because he has a lot of money.
**Having**
acceptedAnswers: Having a lot of money, Ed can afford three holidays abroad each year.
Having a lot of money, he can afford three holidays abroad each year.

items.prompt:
Maria began to worry when she realised she was lost.
**Realising**
acceptedAnswers: Realising she was lost, Maria began to worry.
Realising that she was lost, Maria began to worry.

exercises.title: J · Same subject?
exercises.instruction: If the sentence is already correct, write it again. If it is incorrect, rewrite it so that the participle and the main clause have the same subject.

items.prompt: Looking through the window, a plane was passing overhead.
acceptedAnswers: Looking through the window, I saw a plane passing overhead.
Looking through the window, I saw a plane that was passing overhead.

items.prompt: Realising that it was late, I ran all the way home.
acceptedAnswers: Realising that it was late, I ran all the way home.

items.prompt: Having examined me, I was given a prescription by the doctor.
acceptedAnswers: Having examined me, the doctor gave me a prescription.
Having been examined, I was given a prescription by the doctor.

items.prompt: Turning on the television, the newsreader said there had been an explosion.
acceptedAnswers: Turning on the television, I heard the newsreader say there had been an explosion.
Turning on the television, I heard that there had been an explosion.

items.prompt: Dropping the shopping bags on the kitchen floor, Mrs Moorcroft sighed and sat down heavily.
acceptedAnswers: Dropping the shopping bags on the kitchen floor, Mrs Moorcroft sighed and sat down heavily.

items.prompt: Having practised the piano, I decided to call one of my friends.
acceptedAnswers: Having practised the piano, I decided to call one of my friends.
